_comment: Two caps for two different things. max_survivor_fraction is a one-sided cap on the SAMPLED run's survivor rate (saturable: below 1.0, because a rate in [0,1] can never exceed 1.0). The unpinned-site count is the exact-count ratchet over the DETERMINISTIC inventory -- every candidate site the ratcheted operators generate across the whole tree -- and it is DERIVED, not stored: tests/mutation_table.py counts it here and at the ratchet base (the merge base; HEAD^1 on main) and refuses growth. A site carries a disposition under survivor_triage (a verdict) or killed_by (a driver that kills it), keyed 'FILE:SCOPE KIND DIGEST[#N]' -- the def around the line and sha1 of its `old` text, never its line number -- with both maps kept in key order. After a hand merge of this file, run `python3 tests/mutation_table.py --normalize`. See the header of tests/mutation_table.py.
reason: The ratchet is the exact count of candidate sites with no disposition, derived at both ends and committed nowhere; a site leaves it only by carrying a disposition -- a `killed_by` driver, or a `survivor_triage` verdict (equivalent/gap) pinned to the exact `old` line. Keys moved from FILE:LINE KIND to a content anchor in fix/rca-ledger-anchors, re-derived on its merge of origin/main 4d31d55e on 2026-09-24: `--normalize` mapped all 103 dispositions (21 triage, 82 killed_by) with none unmapped, every entry's value unchanged, and the unpinned set identical under the old and the new code on that tree (3725 of 3828 candidates). The line-keyed re-derivation log main's `reason` had accumulated is superseded: it recorded re-keys this form no longer needs, and it stays in git history. The `last_measured` survivor_lines are a run's table and keep that run's FILE:LINE form. One property the triage entries share, stated here so no reason hides it: tests/entities.py's #1217 mark-staleness self-check reddens when any `survivor_triage`-marked line is mutated, because the mark's pin then names a mutant the tree no longer generates. That is a property of the RECORD, not a behavioural kill, so those sites are survivors here and not `killed_by` entries. The `gap` verdict records a MEASURED survivor and does NOT move the fraction: `survivor_gaps` counts every survivor no triage has called equivalent. The full scope drives neither tests/harness_headers.py nor tests/stress.py (SCOPE_DEFERRED, #1930 (a), R9-RC-NIGHTLY-DEFER): each measures the machine, so its own limits judged a comment-only null control on a shared runner and refused the lane -- harness_headers.py SIGXCPU rc=-24 (run 37108891698), stress.py's own cost budget at 8.0x against 7.9x (run 37189092011). That drop moves no cap here: the count it could have raised is not a stored number (RETIRED since #1577), and the `killed_by` rows naming the pair stay, because a row claims that a driver kills a site and the changed scope still runs that driver. What the drop leaves unre-verified this lane prints in its own census clause (`census_deferral_note`), which names both drivers and how many recorded dispositions name one.
